summary.oneLiner: An "efficiency-first" quarter: management deliberately traded balance-sheet growth for quality, NIM guidance shifted from "defend" to "improve", while pre-building ECL provisions ahead of the FY28 transition.

one-line thesis: An "efficiency-first" quarter: management deliberately traded balance-sheet growth for quality — shedding ~Rs 18,000-20,000 cr of bulk deposits, cutting deposit cost 18 bps, lifting NIM to a cycle-high 2.80% and printing record operating profit (~Rs 8,003 cr) and steady 1.36% ROA. The visible cost is sub-industry credit/deposit growth (CD ratio already stretched to ~86%). The pivot from here is offensive — NIM guidance shifted from "defend" to "improve", a >Rs 1,00,000 cr sanctioned-undisbursed corporate pipeline, RAM growth targeted at 18-20%, and FCNR mobilization of USD 1.5-2 bn by September — while pre-building ECL provisions (Rs 800 cr set aside) ahead of the FY28 transition.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy): > One-offs to flag: Income-tax refund Rs 532 cr (vs Rs 562 cr in Mar-26, Rs 14 cr in Jun-25); PSLC fee Rs 217 cr (vs zero in Jun-25); treasury income down to ~Rs 630-640 cr (from Rs 1,439 cr in Jun-25); NPA provision spiked to ~Rs 2,020 cr (from ~Rs 420 cr in Mar) partly for higher write-offs / tax planning; Rs 100 cr additional ECL buffer added this quarter (Rs 800 cr cumulative).
guidance (critical — verify next quarter: Credit growth: industry + 1% (industry ~18-19%; bank currently ~13-14%); RAM (Retail/Agri/MSME) targeted >18-20%.
Deposit growth: roughly credit growth minus ~2%; CASA+RTD prioritized over bulk; aspire to cut bulk deposit to ~15% of total over 1-3 years.
NIM: improve from 2.80% (upgraded from "defend"); yield on advances to bottom out; deposit-cost reduction to continue.
FCNR / overseas: mobilize USD 1.5-2 bn by September (~Rs 20,000 cr); USD 106 mn done; OFCB USD 200-300 mn planned.
Recovery: Rs 4,500-5,000 cr for FY27 (Rs 750 cr in Q1).
ECLGS disbursement: Rs 14,000-15,000 cr overall (Rs ~10,000 cr done; Rs 12,000 cr sanctioned).
ECL provisioning: total requirement ~Rs 11,300-11,500 cr; carrying ~Rs 5,500 cr additional; ~Rs 6,000 cr remaining to build before the 1-Apr-2027 transition, phaseable over 4 years.
PSLC fee: Rs 800-900 cr full-year aspiration (conditional on Agri/SMF growth).
CD ratio: hold ~85-86%, not much beyond.
order book & pipeline (loan book & liqui: Corporate pipeline: >Rs 1,00,000 cr sanctioned but undisbursed, drawing down in stages; ~Rs 60,000-70,000 cr underwritten over the last 8-9 months and being down-sold. Domestic corporate:RAM mix ~57:43. Liquidity: LCR 121% (board floor 107%, RBI 100%) — ~Rs 42,000 cr surplus (1 bp ≈ Rs 2,000 cr); NSFR comfortable. Deposits taken Rs 30,000-40,000 cr in the quarter despite bulk shedding; CASA avg Rs 24,000+ cr, RTD avg Rs 17,000 cr (total Rs 41,000 cr average build Mar→Jun).
segment / vertical detail: Corporate: self-sustained; selling (not buying) IBPC — "IBPC we do not want to even hear it." Zero-IBPC-buy policy intact.
RAM: cluster scheme + Agri Unnati scheme + MSME/retail schemes to push 18-20% growth; sold good IBPC in Agri (surplus vs earlier deficit) and booked income.

Ecosystem banking vertical: new sourcing engine — 1,200+ RM staff (CGM-led, 7-8 GMs, 14 DGMs), 118 centers, 12 hubs; driving CASA stickiness (95-99% in advances/SB/CA) and NACH registrations up to 18,000/day (from 12-13k).
Gold loan: de-grew ~Rs 2,500-3,000 cr deliberately on compliance/regulatory tightening.
Treasury: income normalized to ~Rs 630-640 cr; AFS reserve improved to -Rs 345 cr (from -Rs 800 cr).
margins & cost dynamics: NIM 2.80% (from 2.64%) driven by: 18 bps deposit-cost reduction (bulk shed, CASA+RTD focus), re-mixing lower-yield to higher-yield advances, and LCR-guideline gains (net +2.5-3% liquidity benefit from lower run-off factors on society/trust AOP deposits). Cost of funds flat ~4.37% held up by legacy high-cost Tier-2 (some at ~9%; Rs 850 cr shed this quarter, Rs 2,500 cr call option to be exercised at ~8.7% blended). Cost-to-income down ~500 bps.
capex / expansion: N/A (bank) — "expansion" is franchise/tech: Project Muskaan transformation showing "green shoots"; ecosystem-banking build-out (people/centers/hubs); EY + Oracle OFSAA engaged for ECL model configuration.
capital allocation: CRAR 18.46% (~Rs 1 lakh cr headroom from capital alone at ~Rs 10,000 cr per 1%). Highest-ever dividend (per prior quarter). Provisioning stance conservative: Rs 800 cr ECL buffer pre-built (outside Tier-2/PCR/profit); write-offs used to clean the book and for tax planning. Calling legacy high-cost Tier-2. No new capital raise flagged as needed.
risks & watch-items: Growth gap: deposit & overall credit growth trailing industry; CD ratio already ~86% limits headroom — funding must accelerate to sustain credit growth.

MSME stress: acknowledged and "going to be there" (economy-linked); concentrated in low-ticket, guarantee-covered/state-sponsored exposures; 140-regional-office MSME customer-meet study (2,500+ MSMEs) as mitigation.
Maharashtra farm-loan waiver: sizable Agri exposure; mgmt expects net-positive on reimbursement (data submitted), no impact felt yet.
ECL transition (1-Apr-2027): ~Rs 6,000 cr more to provide; one-time CRAR hit to ~17.54% if fully absorbed in year one; annual run-rate credit cost still being modeled.
Provision/write-off optics: NPA provision jumped to ~Rs 2,020 cr and PCR dipped — mgmt frames Q1 write-off as one-off/tax-driven, not recurring.
Macro: Russia-Ukraine / West Asia, oil, currency, rate moves.
management quality / tone: Confident, granular, investor-familiar (MD engages analysts by name). Repeated "five pillars" framing (Efficiency, Robustness, Quality & Sustainable Growth, Profitability, Customer Centricity) and "business first, compliance always." Candid on the growth shortfall being a deliberate efficiency trade, and on MSME stress. Some answers meandering/verbose; several exact figures deferred ("we'll get back"). Awards cited (IIBF governance, TransUnion CIBIL data quality, IBA cybersecurity, ET Enterprise Security).
non-obvious takeaways: The weak headline growth is self-inflicted (bulk-deposit shedding + gold-loan de-growth ~Rs 2,500-3,000 cr + cautious CC drawdown as corporates parked ECLGS cash) — not demand loss; sets up a cleaner, higher-margin base.
NIM guidance quietly upgraded from "defend" to "improve" — the key re-rating signal on the call.
Rs 800 cr ECL pre-provisioning (ahead of requirement) + phaseable Rs 6,000 cr residual means the FY28 ECL cliff is largely de-risked — CRAR floor ~17.54% even in a worst-case single-year absorption.
ECLGS uptake (~Rs 10,000 cr) is NOT a stress signal — even large corporates drew it to sit on precautionary cash; it reduced CC balances rather than funding new stress.
PSLC (Rs 217 cr) and income-tax refund (Rs 532 cr) materially flattered fee/other income YoY — normalize when modeling.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers (lis: > Thin on this call (a bank talking to its own book). Only sector-wide dynamics with defensible read-through are mapped; ⭐ = sector knowledge.
qoq change log (fill each quarter): Q1 FY27 (this): Record OP ~Rs 8,003 cr; NIM up to 2.80% (from 2.64%); ROA 1.36%; cost-to-income -500 bps; deposit cost -18 bps. Bulk deposits shed ~Rs 18-20k cr (bulk/total 27%→19%); CD ratio ~86%; CRAR 18.46%. SMA >Rs 5 cr = Rs 2,382 cr (lowest). ECL buffer Rs 800 cr (added Rs 100 cr); NPA provision ~Rs 2,020 cr; write-offs elevated (one-off). NIM guidance upgraded "defend"→"improve". FCNR USD 106 mn done (target 1.5-2 bn by Sept).

Q2 FY27 → check: NIM actually rising vs 2.80%; FCNR mobilization vs USD 1.5-2 bn by Sept; credit growth closing gap to industry+1% / RAM to 18-20%; deposit growth catch-up; ECL residual build (Rs 6,000 cr) pace; MSME/Maharashtra-waiver asset-quality read; PSLC run-rate vs Rs 800-900 cr FY aim; CD ratio held ≤86%.
